sections.overview: This small crane fly belongs to the family Limoniidae; adults are often found in woodland and cave entrances.
sections.identification: The adult is about 9–11 millimetres long, with patterned wings and three dark rings on the yellow front femora.
sections.habitat: It occurs in wooded places and is frequently recorded in the entrance zones of caves and mines, where adults rest during the warmer part of the year.
sections.diet: Larvae have been recorded in several kinds of decomposing material, including leaf mould and rotting wood; their precise feeding habits are not detailed here.
sections.behavior: The adult enters caves temporarily to rest, so it is a trogloxene rather than an obligate cave species.
sections.reproduction: Larvae develop outside the adult cave-roosting sites, in wet organic material such as leaf litter or decaying wood; the sources do not give a single development schedule.
sections.ecology: Its seasonal use of cave entrances links surface woodland habitats with underground spaces; a German cave-conservation group selected it as Cave Animal of the Year 2019.
sections.conservation: The European catalogue and regional records document a broad presence, but the sources reviewed do not establish a global population trend or conservation assessment.
